content_html:
Does your site
sound like AI wrote it?

We crawl every page, flag the exact words and patterns that read as generic AI copy, and show you why: score, evidence, and a rule-grounded rewrite. Free for your whole site.

no signup · no credit card · ~20 seconds

See a sample report

Generic, AI-sounding copy doesn't just read badly. It quietly costs conversions, and after Google's February 2026 core update, it can cost search rankings too. The question isn't whether your site used AI. It's whether it reads as trustworthy, specific writing, or like everyone else's landing page.

// how it works

Two engines. Only one of them ever touches an AI model.

01

Crawl

We fetch every real page on your site. Not a sitemap dump. Nav, footer, and boilerplate get stripped before anything is scored.

02

Detect

A rule-based engine flags stock AI phrases, sentence-length monotony, and generic openers. And the good news, there's zero cost! That's why it's free for the whole site.

03

Fix

Click any flag for a rule-grounded rewrite. Nothing ships automatically. You approve every change before it reaches your dashboard.

ONE-TIME

Rescanning is always free. Publishing regularly? Add the $9.99/mo retainer so every rescan's fixes are covered automatically. No repeat unlock needed. Optional, cancel anytime.

// faq

Questions people actually ask

Isn't this just the free Chrome extension everyone already uses?

Those tools are great for a single paste. We crawl your whole site, track score over time, and hand you a rule-grounded fix; not just a percentage. If a single-page check is genuinely all you need, use that instead.

Will the "fix" just replace one kind of AI writing with another?

The fix engine is grounded in the specific rule that fired plus your sentence. It will never be an open "make this sound human" prompt. You review and approve every suggestion before anything changes.

Do you store my site's content?

A free scan doesn't require an account at all. We keep just enough to show your report and let a link be shareable. Nothing is sold or used to train anything.

Why one-time instead of a subscription?

Re-scanning is free and unlimited on every tier, always. The one-time $20 unlocks fixes for everything flagged today. If you publish regularly, the optional $9.99/mo retainer covers newly-flagged content automatically after every re-scan, so you're never paying twice for the same kind of check-in. Most sites don't need that, so it stays optional.

Are you accusing me of using AI?

No! plenty of flagged writing is human, just generic. The score isn’t "AI probability," it’s "does this read as trustworthy, specific writing," which is the thing that actually affects conversions and rankings.
